age_fit.reason: Warm and concrete in the classroom lessons, but the time lessons use long multi-sentence turns and abstract tips ('the last time is the answer') that are heavy for a 6-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Correct English, targeted b/p spelling hints, then the answer is modelled, and there is a clear progression in the time dialogues (quarter past/to, changed times).

age_fit.reason: Turns are short, but the lesson 1 openings are disjointed and confusing ('I read a book, not I read a bag. You put books in it.'), and 'They get married ___ April' is an odd topic for a 7-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: in/on/at practice is correct, but the lesson 1 prompts and feedback are incoherent (the bag clue, then a sudden 'This is pen' contrast), which a teacher would question.

age_fit.reason: Adult tone, with adult contexts (bus stop, market, neighbour, manager) and nothing childish.

teacher_accept.reason: Present continuous and has/adjective order are taught correctly with models. The tutor probes the learner's adjective-order belief and the learner self-corrects in lesson 4.

age_fit.reason: Short, neutral messages with school and family contexts that suit a teenager, and no talking down.

teacher_accept.reason: Mostly sound practice, but there is wrong or garbled modelling: 'This is my father. He is a doctor. She is a doctor.' and the broken example 'The bag is red." A bag is red.'

age_fit.reason: Plain, respectful tone for an adult. A few prompts (favourite animal, best teacher) are simple but are not childish in delivery.

teacher_accept.reason: there is/are and plural -s are taught correctly, full-sentence answers are modelled, and the tutor scaffolds sensibly when the learner keeps failing.

age_fit.reason: Concise, neutral tone, with family, food and routine contexts that suit a teenager.

teacher_accept.reason: Word-order lessons are solid, but the food lessons have an odd model ('The pasta is a food.') and a questionable correction of 'drinks soup', so there are reservations.

age_fit.reason: Short, warm turns with concrete café, pet and family contexts that suit a 7-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Polite requests with some/a, third-person -s and adverb position are correct and corrected well. One mismatched prompt ('person you know' with Can I have) is a minor slip.

age_fit.reason: Friendly, but turns are long and explanatory (consonant-doubling rule, expensive phones, 'I worked late'), which is more suited to an older learner than an 8-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Comparatives (doubling, more ... than, irregular better) and and/but/because are taught correctly with sensible steps.

age_fit.reason: Mostly short, but some turns are terse and a dense spelling rule ('-es after -sh, -ch, -s, -x, -o; -ies after consonant + y') is too abstract for a 7-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Third-person -s is practised correctly, but the workplace feedback is muddled ('A teacher works in a school... Your word fits a chef.') and repeated misspellings get little real support.

age_fit.reason: Café, shopping and homework contexts and a neutral tone suit a teenager.

teacher_accept.reason: much/many is taught well, but the café lessons have mismatched prompts ('person you know' with Can I have) and vague some/any explanations ('not whether it exists').

age_fit.reason: Short, friendly turns with animals, family and 'quick game' framing that suit a 12-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Lesson 1 leaves 'has hair long black' uncorrected twice, and lesson 4 becomes a weak missing-letter drill. The comparative and adjective-order teaching is otherwise correct.

age_fit.reason: Short, encouraging turns with pets, animals and family that suit an 11-year-old.

teacher_accept.reason: Third-person -s, adverb position and comparatives are taught correctly with clear right/wrong models and useful spelling hints.
